newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strategie Grains raises German winter barley yield.
newsitem.headline: Strategie Grains raises German winter barley yield.

text.p: French analyst Strategie Grains said on Monday it had raised its forecast for German winter barley yields but cut the figure for spring barley yields.
In its report for August the analyst put the 1997 winter barley yield at 6.5 tonnes per hectare against 5.8 tonnes last month and 5.61 tonnes in 1996.
It cut its estimate for spring barley yields to 4.9 tonnes per hectare from 5.1 last month and 5.22 in 1996.
It also raised its forecast for maize yields to 7.7 tonnes per hectare from 7.56 last month and 7.83 in 1996.
It kept its estimate for soft wheat yields unchanged from last month at 7.25 tonnes per hectare against 7.3 tonnes in 1996.
Strategie Grains put the 1997 winter barley crop at 9.3 million tonnes against 7.93 million in 1996, and the spring barley crop at 4.15 million tonnes, unchanged from 1996.
It put the 1997 soft wheat crop at 19.72 million tonnes against 18.88 million in 1996, and the maize crop at 2.84 million tonnes against 2.91 million tonnes last year.

"Almost everywhere winter barley yields sharply exceed those of last year (notably in the Saxony, Brandenburg, and Mecklenburg regions) and the average German yield for that grain will probably exceed, as we had forecast, the weak results of 1996. But it is not certain that the level of 1995 will be reached," it said.
Barley quality results were mixed, with large variations in specific weights while moisture levels were high, ranging from 15 to 20 percent.

Specific weights exceed 60 in Brandenburg, and they were close to 65 in Baden-Wuerttemberg, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia and Rhineland-Palatinate. They were above 62 in Saxony and Thuringia and ranged from 58 to 65 in Saxony-Anhalt.

In early August the soft wheat and rye harvest were just starting in the south and the east. Initial results showed winter wheat in southern Germany had a higher protein content than last year. But protein content was less good in Saar and Rhineland-Palatinate.
For rye, Hagberg numbers were below last year and farmers also expected lower Hagberg numbers for wheat in the south.
The spring barley harvest had started in Baden-Wuerttemberg and initial results showed yields declining by 10 percent compared to last year, but it was premature to say if this indicated a trend.
